Mythbusters - Thermite Vs. Ice

This explains a bit why the ice explodes. I think it's because of the high internal stresses caused by the stupid high thermal gradients, which is for sure what we see in the copper video. I don't personally believe that the high temperatures from the termite causing the hydrogen and oxygen to dissociate are really the primary driver here. Even if it were the case and they were re-oxidizing I don't see it releasing energy in the reaction really on the time scale they're seeing.

Thermite does burn at high enough temperatures to cause the dissociation of water into oxygen and hydrogen. In addition, the combustion reaction of the hydrogen back into water can indeed cause an explosion of that size very quickly (if you have ever worked with sodium metal, or really any pure alkaline metal, you will see this. Potassium especially.) However, I think it far more likely that this is the result of a steam explosion. The temperature of the ice increases rapidly, causing it to very nearly sublimate (there is a liquid phase, but it vanishes so rapidly as to almost not exist). The steam is trapped within the remaining solid body of ice, and its temperature continues to rise, causing an expansion. Eventually, the pressure of the steam overwhelms the solid ice and releases a mechanical explosion. Dissociation may be a contributing factor, but I think it unlikely to be the primary driver.
